original_question: Let 1 < p < infinity, let Omega be a connected open subset of R^n with n >= 2, and let u be a weak solution of the p-Laplace equation div(|grad u|^(p-2) grad u) = 0 in Omega. If u vanishes of infinite order at an interior point x_0 of Omega, must u vanish identically on all of Omega?
target_in_paper: Problem 1.2 (Strong unique continuation) in §1 of the arXiv version; the same statement is renumbered as Problem 2.2 in §2, “Unique continuation for the p-laplacian,” of the published version. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2003.11441))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s target almost verbatim: it has the correct operator div(|∇u|^(p-2)∇u)=0, the correct parameter range 1<p<∞, the ambient setting of a connected open set Ω⊂R^n with n≥2, the weak-solution viewpoint, the hypothesis that u vanishes of infinite order at an interior point x_0∈Ω, and the conclusion u≡0 in Ω. This is exactly the paper’s “strong unique continuation” formulation. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))
missing_details: The section introducing the problem explicitly places weak (variational) solutions in the natural Sobolev space W^{1,p}(Ω); your draft says “weak solution” but does not make that ambient function space explicit. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))

The paper labels this statement as the strong unique continuation problem, so naming that property makes the question more paper-faithful and easier to recognize. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, one should specify what “vanishes of infinite order” means; the paper uses that phrase in the problem statement but does not formalize it in this section. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))

If the aim is to isolate the genuinely open part of the question, the paper immediately records that the answer is known to be positive when p=2 and also when n=2; it says the problem remains open in the case n≥3 and p≠2. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))
refined_question: In the unresolved regime n≥3 and 1<p<∞ with p≠2, let Ω⊂R^n be a connected open set, and let u∈W^{1,p}(Ω) satisfy the weak p-Laplace equation, i.e. ∫_Ω |∇u|^(p-2)∇u·∇φ dx = 0 for every φ∈C_c^∞(Ω). If there exists an interior point x_0∈Ω such that u vanishes of infinite order at x_0, in the sense that for every m>0 one has ∫_{B_r(x_0)} |u|^p dx = O(r^m) as r→0, must u be identically zero in Ω? ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))
justification: The draft is trying to capture the paper’s exact strong unique continuation problem for p-harmonic functions. The section first introduces the p-Laplace equation in a connected open set Ω⊂R^n, 1<p<∞, with weak solutions viewed in W^{1,p}(Ω), and then states the strong unique continuation question exactly in this form. The immediate surrounding discussion adds the key sharpening that the statement is already known for p=2 and for n=2, so the real research content is the case n≥3, p≠2. The only substantial stand-alone detail missing from your draft is an explicit definition of “vanishes of infinite order,” since the paper itself leaves that phrase implicit. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))
